analysis: What changed vs the 6:00 AM premarket brief: the open confirmed the overnight script — tech-led red, Dow flat. SPY opened at $749.66 and sat near $748.46 (-0.78%) by 9:51 AM ET, while the Dow held essentially flat, the same rotation seen Friday. Nvidia bounced off its premarket lows (opened $159.02, ~$160.88 by 9:51 AM ET, -1.2%) after the UBS target cut to $240 and the Ives 'gone for good' pushback — the stock is stabilizing into tomorrow's print rather than cascading, which matters more than the direction of any single headline. The Empire State print (7.8 vs ~17.6 expected) is the day's only hard data so far and it cut both ways: headline momentum cooled sharply from October's 25.5, but the employment index jumped to 18.1, its best since June 2022 — a soft-activity, strong-hiring mix that gives neither the hawks nor the doves a clean read ahead of Warsh at noon. Megacaps are all red in the first half hour, but the spread is wide: Microsoft and Apple down a fraction, Alphabet and Tesla down ~2% — no single new company headline drove the laggards, it's the same AI-trade de-risking into Nvidia's print. Signal vs noise: the Empire State miss is real but a second-tier regional survey; the VIX creeping back over 20 (20.50) and the 10Y holding above 5.1% are the tape's real tells — fear is rising while rates stay restrictive. The CEO-return debate remains sentiment until the board or a filing moves. Tomorrow's Nvidia print is still the week's first hard data point.

headlines.headline: Stocks open lower, tech leading down: SPY opened at $749.66 and traded near $748.46 at 9:51 AM ET (-0.78% vs Friday's $754.37 close). The S&P 500 sat ~-0.3%, the Nasdaq 100 ~-0.83%, while the Dow was essentially flat — the same rotational split as Friday, when the S&P fell 0.40%, the Nasdaq 0.91%, and the Dow rose 0.10%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open confirmed the overnight futures fade rather than reversing it — buyers are still waiting for Tuesday's Nvidia print before stepping in.

headlines.headline: Nvidia steadies off premarket lows into the open: NVDA opened at $159.02 and traded near $160.88 at 9:51 AM ET (-1.2% vs Friday's $162.85 close), after premarket lows near $157. The UBS price-target cut to $240 (from $300) and the Ives 'gone for good' pushback remain the morning's overhang; earnings land Tue Nov 17 after the close (consensus ~$108.9B revenue, ~$2.47 EPS; options imply a ~7% move).
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce off the lows says the selling is pausing into the print, not accelerating — the stock is being held for the numbers, not dumped on the governance fight.

headlines.headline: Empire State manufacturing cools sharply: the NY Fed's November index fell to 7.8 from 25.5 in October, well below the ~17.6-18 consensus. New orders slipped to 3.0, but the employment index jumped to 18.1 — its highest since June 2022 — and the prices-paid index eased to 45.9. Activity still grew, just far more slowly than October's surge.
headlines.why_it_matters: A soft headline with strong hiring underneath — a mixed read that gives neither rate hawks nor doves a clean signal ahead of Warsh's noon remarks.

headlines.headline: Megacaps all red in the first half hour, but split wide: GOOGL -2.19% to ~$289.30, TSLA -1.95% to ~$382.62, AMZN -1.58% to ~$262.45, META -1.28% to ~$633.51, NVDA -1.21%, AAPL -0.42% to ~$354.78, MSFT -0.21% to ~$522.78 (Finnhub, ~9:51 AM ET). No fresh company-specific headline drove the laggards — broad AI-trade de-risking into Nvidia's print.
headlines.why_it_matters: The spread between the resilient pair (Microsoft, Apple) and the rest shows the selling is selective, not a blanket exit — names without a fresh overhang are holding up best.

headlines.headline: VIX creeps back above 20 as yields hold over 5%: the VIX traded ~20.50 at 9:19 AM ET, up ~1.2 points from Friday's 19.30 close (+6.22%). The 10-year Treasury yield sat ~5.14%, down ~1 bp from Friday's 5.15% close. Gold ~$3,867 (-0.43%) and Bitcoin ~$64,384 (-1.41%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Fear is rising while rates stay restrictive — the combination that keeps growth multiples under pressure until either Nvidia's print or Warsh's tone gives the tape a reason to relax.
